question: Who wrote the novel ‘Train to Pakistan’?
solution:
The Correct Answer is __Khushwant Singh__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Khushwant Singh's historical novel Train to Pakistan was released in 1956.
 
• It tells the story of **India's partition in August 1947** through the eyes of Mano Majra, a fictional border village.
 
• In** 1998, a film based on this novel with the same title, Train to Pakistan, was released.**
 
• A play based on this novel with the same title "Train to Pakistan" was staged at Lamakaan, an open cultural space in Hyderabad, India, with the first chapter "Dacoity." 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vikram Seth** 

 
 
• Vikram Seth is a **renowned Indian author, poet, and travel writer.**
 
• Born in 1952 in Kolkata, **he is best known for his epic novel *A Suitable Boy*.**
 
• Seth’s works cover a wide range of genres including poetry, novels, and travel writing.
 
• His** writing is known for its lyrical beauty and deep engagement with themes of love, family, and societal issues.**
 
• **Other Books:** **The Golden Gate, From Heaven Lake: Travels through Sinkiang and Tibet, An Equal Music, Two Lives**
 
 
 
• **Mulk Raj Anand**
 
 
• Mulk Raj Anand (1905-2004) **was an Indian writer in English.**
 
• He was well known for his novels that address social issues, particularly the plight of the marginalized and underprivileged.
 
• He** was one of the pioneers of Indian writing in English**, and his works were instrumental in representing the struggles of the oppressed classes in India during the British colonial era.
 
• **Books:** **Untouchable, Coolie, The Private Life of an Indian Prince, The Big Heart, The Road**
 
 
 
• **Bhisham Sahni **
 
 
• **Bhisham Sahni (1915-2003) was an Indian writer, playwright, and actor.**
 
• He is **best known for his novel *Tamas*, w**hich deals with the aftermath of the partition of India in 1947.
 
• Sahni’s works often explore themes of social justice, human suffering, and the political turmoil in post-colonial India.
 
• He was **also involved in theatre and worked as a translator.**
